'''''Krigia cespitosa''''', known as '''common dwarf-dandelion''',<ref name=FNA/> ''' opposite-leaved dwarf-dandelion''',<ref name=FNA/> or '''weedy dwarfdandelion''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=KRCA|taxon=Krigia caespitosa|accessdate=9 August 2015}}</ref> is a North American species of plant in the family [[Asteraceae]] . It is native to northeastern Mexico ([[Nuevo León]]) and to the southeastern and south-central United States, from [[Florida]] to [[Texas]] and north as far as southeastern [[Nebraska]], southern [[Illinois]], and central [[West Virginia]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://plants.usda.gov/plant-profile?symbol=KRBI |title=United States Department of Agriculture plants profile |access-date=2015-08-07 |archive-date=2015-04-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150417111222/http://plants.usda.gov/core/profile?symbol=KRBI |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Krigia%20caespitosa.png |title=Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map, ''Krigia caespitosa'' |access-date=2015-08-07 |archive-date=2015-10-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151015060126/http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Krigia%20caespitosa.png |url-status=live }}</ref>

''Krigia cespitosa'' is an annual herb up to 42 cm (16.8 inches) tall. One plant generally produces one flower head per flower stalk, each head with 12–35 yellow ray flowers but no disc flowers.<ref name=FNA>{{Cite web |url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250067030 |title=Flora of North America, ''Krigia cespitosa'' (Rafinesque) K. L. Chambers, 1973.  Common or opposite-leaved dwarfdandelion |access-date=2015-08-07 |archive-date=2015-09-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924143948/http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250067030 |url-status=live }}</ref>
